title: Where to stick your FASTag on the windshield, and why it won't read
metaTitle: Where to stick FASTag on the windshield (with diagram)
description: The correct FASTag position is inside the windshield, top centre, behind the rear-view mirror. See the diagram, the mistakes that get a tag blacklisted or charged double, and what to do when it won't read.
card: The exact spot on the windshield, how to fix it so it reads first time, and the mistakes that get a tag blacklisted.
checkedAgainst: NHAI affixation procedure, IHMCL circular, PIB releases
lede: Most "FASTag not reading" problems at the plaza start with where and how the tag was stuck. Here is the official position, shown on a diagram, and the fixes when it still won't read.
quickAnswer: Stick the FASTag **from inside the car, at the top centre of the front windshield, behind the rear-view mirror**, with the adhesive side facing outward. Clean and dry the glass first, press it on once, and don't move it afterwards. A tag kept on the dashboard, held in hand or fixed with tape can be **blacklisted** and charged **double toll**.

blocks.caption: Inside the front windshield, top centre, just behind the rear-view mirror. Based on NHAI's affixation procedure.

blocks.text: NHAI's procedure for fixing a FASTag asks for the tag to go **on the inside of the windshield, at the top middle, behind the rear-view mirror**. The reader at the toll lane looks at that part of the glass, so a tag anywhere else is read late, read badly or not read at all.
Fix the tag from inside the vehicle at the top middle of the windshield behind the rear-view mirror, adhesive side facing outward. Once pasted, do not remove or reposition it.

source.title: NHAI – Standard procedure for FASTag affixation

blocks.text: If a dashcam or mirror mount leaves no room right behind the mirror, ICICI Bank's guidance is to place it slightly towards the passenger side, still near the top of the glass. That's bank guidance, not an NHAI rule, so stay as close to the centre as you can.

sections.heading: How to fix it so it reads first time

items.title: Clean the glass from inside
items.text: Wipe the spot behind the mirror and let it dry fully. NHAI's procedure says not to paste the tag on dirty or wet glass.

items.title: Peel the backing just before you stick it
items.text: Don't touch the adhesive with your fingers; dust and oil weaken it.

items.title: Place it once, adhesive side out
items.text: Line it up behind the mirror, then press gently from the centre outwards so there are no air bubbles.

items.title: Leave it alone
items.text: Don't peel it off to adjust it later. A FASTag is built so that lifting it damages the antenna inside, and NHAI's procedure says not to reposition it.

items.title: Don't add tape or glue
items.text: If the tag's own adhesive isn't holding, return it to your bank and ask for a replacement instead of taping it. Tape is one of the listed reasons for blacklisting.

sections.heading: Mistakes that get a tag blacklisted or charged double

items: **Keeping the tag on the dashboard or holding it up at the booth.** NHAI calls these "loose" or "tag-in-hand" FASTags. Since July 2025 toll agencies report them to NHAI for blacklisting or hotlisting.
**Fixing it with cello tape or extra glue**, or sticking it on a separate piece of glass or another surface. An IHMCL circular lists these as reasons a tag can't be used and should be blacklisted.

**Sticking it somewhere other than the front windshield.** Since July 2024 a vehicle entering the toll lane with a tag not fixed on the windshield from inside pays **double the toll**, and the plaza records CCTV of the number plate.
**Placing it behind a metal part or another sticker.** Metal blocks the radio signal. ICICI Bank advises keeping the tag clear of any metallic surface or other sticker.

blocks.text: A vehicle entering a toll lane without a FASTag affixed on the front windshield from inside will be charged double the user fee, and such a FASTag can be blacklisted.

source.title: PIB – NHAI to charge double toll from vehicles with non-affixed FASTag (18 Jul 2024)

sections.heading: Your tag still won't read? Check these in order

items.title: Check the status, not just the sticker
items.text: A tag that's blacklisted, hotlisted or out of balance looks exactly like a working tag. Check it first with our [FASTag status check](/tools/fastag-status), then see [what each status means](/guides/fastag-blacklisted).

items.title: Check the position
items.text: If it sits low on the glass, in a corner or behind a mount, that's likely the cause. You can't move it, so ask your bank for a replacement and fix the new one in the right place.

items.title: Check for damage
items.text: A tag that was peeled, folded or scratched across the chip may never read again. NHAI's FAQ says to approach your issuing bank for a replacement in that case.

items.title: Got a new windshield?
items.text: The old tag can't be peeled off and reused, so you'll need a replacement tag. See [how to replace or reissue a FASTag](/guides/fastag-replacement-reissue).

blocks.title: Tag doesn't beep
blocks.text: If your tag is valid and has enough balance but the plaza's own reader fails, the rules let you cross without paying and you get a zero-transaction receipt. Details in [toll without a working FASTag](/guides/toll-without-fastag-penalty).

faqs.q: Should the FASTag be on the driver's side or the passenger side?
faqs.a: Neither. NHAI's procedure puts it at the top middle of the windshield, behind the rear-view mirror. Only if there's no room there, place it slightly towards the passenger side near the top.

faqs.q: Can I stick the FASTag outside the windshield?
faqs.a: No. It goes on the inside of the glass, adhesive side facing out, so the reader sees it through the windshield.

faqs.q: Can I remove my FASTag and stick it again?
faqs.a: No. NHAI's procedure says not to peel off or reposition a fixed tag. Lifting it usually damages the tag, so you'll need a replacement from your bank.

faqs.q: Is it OK to keep the FASTag on the dashboard?
faqs.a: No. A loose tag or a tag held in hand can be reported to NHAI and blacklisted, and since July 2024 a vehicle with a tag not fixed on the windshield is charged double toll.

faqs.q: How long does a FASTag last?
faqs.a: NHAI's FAQ gives the physical tag a validity of 5 years.

sources.title: NHAI – Standard procedure for FASTag affixation

PIB – NHAI strengthens reporting of 'loose FASTag'
IHMCL policy circular on improper affixing

title: FASTag Annual Pass: price, roads it covers and how trips are counted
description: The FASTag Annual Pass costs ₹3,075 from 1 April 2026 and covers 200 trips or one year at NH and National Expressway plazas. Who can buy it, where it works, how a trip is counted and how to activate it.
card: ₹3,075 for 200 trips or one year on national highways. Who qualifies, where it works and how trips are counted.
checkedAgainst: Gazette G.S.R. 388(E), IHMCL Annual Pass FAQ, PIB releases
lede: One payment a year instead of a toll every crossing. Before you buy, check that your car qualifies and that your regular route actually runs through NHAI plazas.
quickAnswer: The FASTag Annual Pass costs **₹3,075 from 1 April 2026** (₹3,000 before). It's valid for **200 trips or one year, whichever comes first**, only at **national highway and national expressway** fee plazas, and only for **private (non-commercial) cars, jeeps and vans** with a working FASTag. Buy it in the **Rajmargyatra app** or on the NHAI website; it activates on your existing FASTag, normally within 2 hours.

sections.heading: At a glance

head: Annual Pass
rows: ₹3,075 from 1 Apr 2026 (₹3,000 from launch to 31 Mar 2026)
200 trips or 1 year, whichever is earlier
Private car, jeep or van, checked against VAHAN
NH and National Expressway fee plazas only
No, it activates on your existing eligible FASTag
No, only for the vehicle the tag is fixed on
blocks.note: The fee can be revised every year from 1 April (NH Fee Rules, rule 9(3C)).

blocks.text: A non-commercial vehicle with a valid, functional FASTag can get a pass valid for one year or two hundred crossings, whichever is earlier. In a closed tolling system, entry and exit count as a single crossing.

sections.heading: Does your vehicle qualify?

items: **Private car, jeep or van only.** NHAI checks the vehicle against the VAHAN database. Using the pass in a commercial vehicle leads to immediate deactivation without notice.
**The tag must carry your registration number.** Tags registered only on a chassis number aren't eligible until the vehicle number is updated with your bank.
**The tag must be fixed on the windshield**, linked to a valid vehicle number and not blacklisted. If you're unsure, run a [FASTag status check](/tools/fastag-status) first.
**You don't need a new FASTag.** The pass is added to the tag you already have.

sections.heading: Where it works, and where it doesn't

blocks.text: At launch on 15 August 2025 the pass worked at about **1,150 NHAI fee plazas** on national highways and national expressways. On expressways and state highways run by state governments or local bodies, and in parking lots, your FASTag works as a normal tag and the toll is deducted as usual.
Many popular routes mix NHAI plazas with state-run ones. Before you pay ₹3,075, check that the plazas on your regular route are NHAI plazas, or you may still pay at several of them.

sections.heading: How a trip is counted

head: Type of plaza
What counts as one trip
rows: Each crossing is one trip, so going and coming back is two trips
Closed tolling (entry and exit points, like some expressways)
One entry plus its exit is one trip

blocks.text: If you also hold a local pass or monthly pass at a plaza, crossings at that plaza aren't counted against your Annual Pass.

sections.heading: How to buy and activate it

items.title: Open Rajmargyatra or the NHAI website
items.text: These are the only two official places to buy the pass.

items.title: Enter your vehicle number
items.text: The system checks that the vehicle is a private car, jeep or van and that your FASTag is active.

items.title: Pay ₹3,075
items.text: Pay by UPI, card or net banking. You **can't** pay from your FASTag wallet balance.

items.title: Wait for the SMS
items.text: The pass activates on your existing FASTag, normally within 2 hours of payment.

blocks.text: You can also buy it for someone else's car: in Rajmargyatra use **Add Pass**, enter their vehicle number and verify with the OTP sent to their number.

sections.heading: When it runs out

blocks.text: After 200 trips or one year, your tag automatically goes back to being a normal FASTag and tolls are deducted from your balance again. To continue, buy the pass again. Keep some balance on the tag anyway: plazas outside the scheme still deduct the normal toll.

faqs.q: What is the FASTag Annual Pass price in 2026?
faqs.a: ₹3,075 from 1 April 2026, revised from ₹3,000. NHAI announced the revision on 15 March 2026.

faqs.q: Is the FASTag Annual Pass valid on state highways and state expressways?
faqs.a: No. It works only at NH and National Expressway fee plazas. On roads run by state governments or local bodies, the normal toll is deducted from your FASTag.

faqs.q: Can I use the Annual Pass on a taxi or commercial vehicle?
faqs.a: No. It's only for private cars, jeeps and vans. Use in a commercial vehicle leads to immediate deactivation without notice.

faqs.q: Can I pay for the Annual Pass from my FASTag balance?
faqs.a: No. It's paid separately through the Rajmargyatra app or the NHAI website.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund if I don't use all 200 trips?
faqs.a: NHAI's FAQ doesn't cover refunds, and banks such as Axis and IDFC FIRST say no refund applies. Treat it as non-refundable.

faqs.q: Do I need a new FASTag for the Annual Pass?
faqs.a: No. It's added to your existing FASTag if that tag is eligible, active and linked to your vehicle number.

tools.label: Estimate your toll without the pass

title: FASTag KYV: do you still need it, and how to finish it
metaTitle: FASTag KYV 2026: who still needs it and how to do it
description: KYV (Know Your Vehicle) is no longer a routine requirement for cars since 1 February 2026. When you still need it, what to upload (one front photo) and what to do if your FASTag was deactivated.
card: Cars mostly don't need KYV any more. When you still do, what to upload and how to get a deactivated tag working.
checkedAgainst: PIB releases (Oct 2025, Jan 2026), NPCI KYV guidelines, IHMCL KYC FAQ
lede: KYV used to switch off thousands of car FASTags. The rules have eased twice since then. Here's what applies to your vehicle today.
quickAnswer: For **cars, jeeps and vans, KYV is no longer a routine requirement**. New car tags issued from **1 February 2026** don't need it, and existing car tags need it only if there's a complaint, such as a loose tag or misuse. If your bank does ask, you usually upload **one front photo showing the number plate and the FASTag**; RC details are fetched from VAHAN. **Commercial vehicles** still go through KYV.

sections.heading: What KYV is

blocks.text: KYV (Know Your Vehicle) checks that a FASTag is on the vehicle it was issued for. It came from NPCI's June 2024 guidelines, which asked banks to verify vehicle details against VAHAN and collect vehicle photos, and to blacklist tags that weren't verified.

head: When
What changed
rows: KYV rules start: front and side photos, tags linked to a mobile number
Simplified: car side photo dropped, only a front photo with number plate and FASTag; RC fetched from VAHAN; tags not cut off without warning
Dropped for new car/jeep/van tags; existing car tags need KYV only after a complaint; tags activate only after VAHAN validation

blocks.text: From 1 February 2026, KYV is discontinued for new FASTags issued to cars, jeeps and vans. For existing car FASTags, KYV is no longer a routine requirement and applies only where complaints arise, such as loose FASTags, incorrect issuance or misuse.

source.title: PIB – KYV discontinued for cars on new FASTags (1 Jan 2026)

sections.heading: Who still needs KYV

items: **Commercial vehicles** (trucks, buses, LCVs): no 2026 change was announced for them, so KYV still applies.
**Cars with a complaint against the tag**, for example a tag reported as loose, issued on the wrong vehicle or misused.
**Cars where VAHAN has no data** for the vehicle: the bank then validates using your RC instead.

sections.heading: How to complete KYV when your bank asks

items.title: Open your issuer's FASTag portal or app
items.text: Use the portal of the bank that issued your tag. For tags issued directly by NHAI, the IHMCL FAQ points to fastag.ihmcl.com.

items.title: Take one clear front photo
items.text: Stand in front of the vehicle so the number plate and the FASTag on the windshield are both visible. Since October 2025 a side photo isn't needed for cars.

items.title: Let it fetch your RC
items.text: RC details are pulled from VAHAN using your vehicle, chassis or mobile number. Upload the RC only if the portal asks for it.

items.title: Keep the reference number
items.text: If the tag stays inactive after a few days, call your bank with it, then the national highway helpline **1033**.

blocks.text: If your FASTag is fixed on the dashboard or held in hand, the front photo will show it. Stick it properly first: see [where to stick your FASTag](/guides/where-to-stick-fastag).

sections.heading: If your tag was deactivated for KYV

blocks.text: Since the October 2025 change, banks are expected to send SMS reminders and help you before disconnecting a tag, and FASTag service isn't supposed to stop without giving you a chance to complete KYV. No fixed number of days has been published. If your tag shows as blacklisted, complete KYV through the steps above, then check the status again after it's approved. See [what each FASTag status means](/guides/fastag-blacklisted).

faqs.q: Is FASTag KYV mandatory in 2026?
faqs.a: Not for most cars. New car, jeep and van tags issued from 1 February 2026 don't need it, and existing car tags need it only after a complaint. Commercial vehicles still need it.

faqs.q: What photos are needed for FASTag KYV?
faqs.a: For cars, one front photo showing the number plate and the FASTag on the windshield. The side photo was dropped in October 2025.

faqs.q: Do I need to upload my RC for KYV?
faqs.a: Usually not. RC details are fetched automatically from VAHAN. The bank asks for the RC only when VAHAN has no data for the vehicle.

faqs.q: My FASTag was blacklisted for KYV. How long until it works again?
faqs.a: It's reactivated once your bank approves the KYV. No fixed timeline is published; if it's still inactive after a few days, call your bank and then the 1033 helpline.

sources.title: PIB – KYV discontinued for cars on new FASTags
NPCI – Customer onboarding and Re-KYV guidelines

title: Blacklisted, hotlisted or low balance: what each FASTag status means
metaTitle: FASTag blacklisted, hotlisted, low balance: meaning & fix
description: What blacklisted, hotlisted, low balance, exempted and closed mean on a FASTag, why a tag gets blacklisted, the 60-minute rule at the plaza, and how to fix each one.
card: The six FASTag status codes in plain words, why tags get blacklisted, and the fix for each cause.
checkedAgainst: NPCI exception codes, NHAI FAQ, PIB clarifications
lede: The toll reader doesn't care how new your tag looks. It checks one thing: the tag's status. Here's what each status means and how to clear it.
quickAnswer: A **blacklisted** FASTag has been blocked by the issuing bank and can't pay toll. Common reasons are **low or negative balance, an incomplete KYC/KYV, a wrong vehicle number, a loose tag or more than one tag on the vehicle**. **Low balance** clears as soon as you recharge. The other causes clear only after you fix them with your bank. Check your tag's status first, then use the table below.

sections.heading: The six statuses a toll reader sees

head: Status
What it means
Fix
rows: Balance is below the level needed for the toll
Blocked by the issuing bank, or on request of RBI, IHMCL/NHAI or law enforcement
Fix the reason with your bank (table below)
Blocked at the issuer level, for example for a negative balance or a violation
Call your bank; clear the dues or complaint
Nothing to fix; no toll is charged
The account was closed, the tag surrendered or moved to a new bank
Use your newest active tag, or buy one
A code NPCI added in 2022 for specific vehicle categories
Ask your bank what it applies to
blocks.note: Codes from NPCI's NETC exception-code circular (2022). NPCI's site blocks direct access, so definitions are summarised from its published circular; confirm the exact wording with your bank.

blocks.text: Run a [FASTag status check](/tools/fastag-status) with your vehicle number to see every tag linked to the vehicle and its status.

sections.heading: Why a FASTag gets blacklisted, and the fix for each

head: Reason
How to fix it
rows: Recharge enough to clear the negative amount plus the next toll
Finish it in your bank's FASTag portal. See [FASTag KYV](/guides/fastag-kyv)
Wrong or invalid vehicle number on the tag
Ask your bank to update the vehicle number using your RC. NHAI told banks in April 2026 to blacklist tags with incorrect numbers
Tag issued on chassis number, never updated
Update the vehicle number within 90 days of issue, or the tag is closed and you need a new one
Loose tag or tag held in hand
Stick it on the windshield properly; if it's damaged, get a [replacement](/guides/fastag-replacement-reissue)
More than one tag on the vehicle
Only the newest tag stays active (One Vehicle One FASTag). Close the older ones
Vehicle class doesn't match the tag
Get a tag of the right class. See [vehicle classes](/guides/fastag-vehicle-class)
Unpaid e-notice from a barrier-free (MLFF) plaza
Pay the pending e-notice; unpaid dues may lead to blacklisting

sections.heading: Recharged just before the plaza? The 60-minute rule

blocks.text: Since 17 February 2025, NPCI's rule says a transaction is declined if the tag was blacklisted, hotlisted or low on balance for **more than 60 minutes before** the reader read it **and** still in that state **10 minutes after**. In practice, if you recharge and the status clears before the plaza, or within about 10 minutes after the read, the toll goes through.

NHAI clarified that the rule concerns disputes between banks and has no impact on customers: all NH plazas check tag status in real time, so you can recharge any time before crossing. Some state highway plazas still refresh status periodically, so recharge a little earlier there.

source.title: PIB – clarification on new FASTag rule (19 Feb 2025)

sections.heading: If it happens at the toll booth

blocks.title: Tag shown as blacklisted
blocks.text: Ask the operator what status the system shows. If it's low balance, recharge from your phone and ask them to read the tag again. If your tag is valid with enough balance but shown as blacklisted wrongly, note the time and plaza and complain to your bank and to 1033.
If you end up paying without FASTag, the extra charge depends on how you pay. See [toll without a working FASTag](/guides/toll-without-fastag-penalty).

faqs.q: What does blacklisted mean on FASTag?
faqs.a: The tag has been blocked by the issuing bank and can't pay toll until the reason is fixed. Common reasons are low or negative balance, incomplete KYC/KYV, a wrong vehicle number, a loose tag or multiple tags on the vehicle.

faqs.q: What is the difference between blacklist and hotlist on FASTag?
faqs.a: Both block the tag at the plaza. A hotlist is an issuer-level block, for example for a negative balance or a violation. A blacklist can also be requested by RBI, IHMCL/NHAI or law enforcement.

faqs.q: How long does it take to remove a FASTag from the blacklist?
faqs.a: A low-balance block clears almost as soon as you recharge. Blocks for KYC, vehicle number or a loose tag clear only after your bank verifies the fix; there's no fixed published time.

faqs.q: Can I check if my FASTag is blacklisted?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the [FASTag status check](/tools/fastag-status) with your vehicle number, or NPCI's NETC status page, or your bank's app.

sources.title: NPCI – Changes to the rule for declining transactions from tags in exception (004A)
PIB – clarification on new FASTag rule
PIB – NHAI validates vehicle registration numbers

title: Wrong or double toll deduction: how to get your money back
metaTitle: FASTag wrong or double deduction: how to get a refund
description: Charged twice, charged for a plaza you never crossed, or charged the wrong amount? How to raise a FASTag dispute with your bank, the reporting windows, typical refund times and when to escalate to 1033.
card: Charged twice or at the wrong plaza? Report it in time, keep the right proof, and know when to escalate.
checkedAgainst: IHMCL FAQ, NHAI FAQ, bank dispute pages
lede: Wrong deductions are fixed through your bank, not at the plaza. What matters most is reporting it within your bank's window, with the SMS as proof.
quickAnswer: Report the wrong deduction to **the bank that issued your FASTag** (app, website or toll-free number) **as soon as you see the SMS**. Banks set their own windows, as short as **15 days** at some banks, so don't wait. The bank raises a chargeback on the toll plaza's bank; IHMCL says this **normally takes 20 to 30 working days**. If your bank doesn't respond, call the national highway helpline **1033**, then email **etc.nodal@ihmcl.com**.

sections.heading: Which problem do you have?

head: What happened
Is it refundable?
What to do
rows: Charged twice at the same plaza for one crossing
Yes, the duplicate is reversed once proven
Raise a dispute with your bank
Charged at a plaza you never crossed
Yes, if the plaza can't show your vehicle crossed
Raise a dispute; mention where your vehicle actually was
Charged at the wrong vehicle class
Dispute it, and fix the tag's class. See [vehicle classes](/guides/fastag-vehicle-class)
Paid by FASTag and also in cash or UPI at the booth
Keep the booth receipt and dispute the FASTag debit
Valid tag not read, and you were made to pay
You shouldn't have paid at all
See [toll without a working FASTag](/guides/toll-without-fastag-penalty), then complain to 1033

sections.heading: How to raise the dispute

items.title: Find the SMS for the deduction
items.text: Every FASTag debit sends an SMS with the plaza, date, time and amount. That's your main evidence.

items.title: Report it to your issuing bank
items.text: Use the bank's FASTag app, website or toll-free number. Mention the transaction ID or SMS details, and what was wrong.

items.title: Attach proof if asked
items.text: Plaza receipt or zero-transaction receipt, the cash or UPI receipt if you paid twice, your RC, and a front photo of the vehicle showing the tag.

items.title: Note the complaint number
items.text: You'll need it to follow up or escalate.

items.title: Escalate if there's no answer
items.text: Call **1033**, the national highway helpline. If your bank still doesn't respond, email **etc.nodal@ihmcl.com** with the complaint number.

sections.heading: How long you have, and how long it takes

head: Bank
Report within
Refund time stated
blocks.note: Banks publish different windows, so follow your own bank's. Checked on each bank's FASTag page in October 2026.

blocks.text: Kotak notes that if the toll plaza's bank later re-claims the amount with proof, a refunded amount can be debited again. Keep your evidence until the case is closed.

sections.heading: Spotting it early

items: Keep FASTag SMS alerts on, and check them the same day after a long trip.
Note plazas where you paid in cash or UPI, and keep those receipts.
Make sure only one FASTag is active on your vehicle; old tags can cause confusing deductions. See [FASTag status meanings](/guides/fastag-blacklisted).
Track an open complaint with our [dispute tracker](/tools/dispute-tracker).

faqs.q: How do I get a refund for a double FASTag deduction?
faqs.a: Report it to the bank that issued your FASTag with the SMS details. The bank raises a chargeback on the plaza's bank and reverses the duplicate once it's proven, normally within 20 to 30 working days.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to report a wrong FASTag deduction?
faqs.a: It depends on your bank: HDFC says 15 days, ICICI 30 days, Kotak 35 days, and IHMCL's general guidance is 40 days. Report it as soon as you see the SMS.

faqs.q: Who do I complain to if my bank doesn't refund a FASTag deduction?
faqs.a: Call the national highway helpline 1033, then email etc.nodal@ihmcl.com with your bank complaint number.

faqs.q: Can the toll plaza refund a wrong FASTag deduction?
faqs.a: No. FASTag refunds go through the bank that issued your tag, which recovers the money from the plaza's bank.

title: Replace, reissue or get a duplicate FASTag (Axis, ICICI, HDFC and others)
metaTitle: FASTag replacement & duplicate tag: fees by bank
description: How to replace a damaged, lost or mismatched FASTag, what each bank charges (Axis ₹100, ICICI ₹99.12, HDFC ₹100, IDFC FIRST ₹100, Kotak nil), the Axis Bank replacement steps, and what happens to your old tag.
card: Damaged, lost or wrong-class tag? Replacement steps, each bank's fee, and the full Axis Bank process.
checkedAgainst: Bank fee pages, Axis Bank FASTag page, NHAI FAQ, NPCI closure policy
lede: A replacement keeps your FASTag account and balance and gives you a new sticker. You need one more often than you'd think: a new windshield, a peeled tag or a class mismatch all mean a new tag.
quickAnswer: Ask **the bank that issued your FASTag** for a replacement. Most banks charge **about ₹100** (Axis ₹100, ICICI ₹99.12, HDFC ₹100, IDFC FIRST ₹100; Kotak charges nothing) and usually ask for your **RC**. Your balance moves to the new tag, and the old one is closed: only one FASTag can be active on a vehicle. At **Axis Bank**, request it at **fastag.axis.bank.in → Helpdesk → Replacement**, or call **1800 419 8585**.

head: Bank
Replacement / reissue fee

Not published on SBI's FASTag pages; ask SBI

sections.heading: Axis Bank: replacement step by step

blocks.text: Axis Bank still issues new FASTags in 2026. Its replacement request covers three cases: damaged, stolen or mismatched tag.

items.title: Log in at fastag.axis.bank.in
items.text: Use the customer portal for your Axis FASTag account.

items.title: Open Helpdesk
items.text: Go to **Helpdesk → Request Information/Queries**.

items.title: Choose the request type
items.text: Type **Request**, sub-type **Replacement**, then pick damaged, stolen or mismatched.

items.title: Upload your RC
items.text: The RC upload is mandatory. The fee is ₹100 including taxes.

items.title: Fix the new tag properly
items.text: Stick it behind the rear-view mirror on clean, dry glass. See [where to stick your FASTag](/guides/where-to-stick-fastag).

head: Axis Bank FASTag
blocks.note: From Axis Bank's FASTag page, checked October 2026. Axis doesn't issue FASTags for two-wheelers.

sections.heading: What happens to your old tag

blocks.text: Under the One Vehicle One FASTag rule, only the latest tag on a vehicle stays active. NPCI's policy auto-closes older duplicate tags 15 days after a new tag is registered for the same vehicle. Your balance is transferred to the new account. Remove and destroy the old sticker so it isn't read by mistake.

blocks.title: Waiting for the new tag
blocks.text: Until the new tag arrives, your old tag may still work if it reads. If it doesn't read and you pay by UPI, the no-FASTag charge applies. See [toll without a working FASTag](/guides/toll-without-fastag-penalty).

sections.heading: Switching bank without a new tag (OneTag)

blocks.text: Since 17 September 2026, the Rajmargyatra app lets you move your FASTag to another bank and **keep the same physical tag and Tag ID**. You check eligibility with your vehicle number, get a 6-digit Mobile Verification Code from your current bank, pick the new bank and finish its KYC and wallet setup. The old bank closes your old wallet and refunds the balance after adjustments. You can't port again for 6 months.
OneTag lets FASTag users change their issuer bank while keeping the same FASTag and Tag ID, through the Rajmargyatra app.

source.title: PIB – Rajmargyatra app hosts 'OneTag' portability (17 Sep 2026)

faqs.q: How do I get a duplicate FASTag from Axis Bank?
faqs.a: Log in at fastag.axis.bank.in, go to Helpdesk → Request Information/Queries, choose Request → Replacement, select damaged, stolen or mismatched, and upload your RC. The fee is ₹100. You can also call 1800 419 8585.

faqs.q: What is the FASTag replacement charge?
faqs.a: About ₹100 at most banks: Axis ₹100, ICICI ₹99.12, HDFC ₹100 and IDFC FIRST ₹100. Kotak charges nothing for reissuance.

faqs.q: Will I lose my FASTag balance if I replace the tag?
faqs.a: No. NHAI's FAQ says the issuer transfers the balance to your new account.

faqs.q: Do I need a new FASTag after changing the windshield?
faqs.a: Yes. A fixed tag can't be peeled off and reused, so ask your bank for a replacement.

faqs.q: Can I change my FASTag bank without buying a new tag?
faqs.a: Yes, since 17 September 2026, using OneTag in the Rajmargyatra app. You keep the same tag and Tag ID.

title: Selling your car? How to close or move your FASTag
metaTitle: Selling your car? How to close your FASTag
description: A FASTag can't be transferred to a new owner. How the seller closes the tag and gets the balance and security deposit back, what the buyer must do, and how OneTag differs from a transfer.
card: A FASTag doesn't go with the car. What the seller closes, what the buyer buys, and how to get your deposit back.
checkedAgainst: NHAI FAQ, Axis Bank and SBI FASTag pages, NPCI closure policy
lede: The FASTag is linked to your bank account and your name, not just the car. If you sell the car without closing it, tolls the new owner runs up can still come out of your wallet.
quickAnswer: A FASTag **can't be transferred to the car's new owner**. The **seller closes the FASTag account** with the bank that issued it and gets the unused balance (and usually the security deposit) refunded. The **buyer removes the old sticker and buys a new FASTag** in their own name. Only one tag can be active on a vehicle, so the buyer's new tag replaces yours.

sections.heading: If you're selling the car

items.title: Recharge or settle any negative balance
items.text: Banks won't close an account with dues. SBI, for example, asks you to settle a negative balance first.

items.title: Ask your bank to close the FASTag account
items.text: Use the bank's FASTag portal or helpline. At Axis Bank, email etc.management@axis.bank.in from your registered email with a cancelled cheque.

items.title: Remove and destroy the sticker
items.text: Axis Bank asks you to remove (destroy) the tag when you sell the vehicle, so it can't be used again.

items.title: Get the refund
items.text: The unused balance goes back to your bank account. Axis says within 10 working days. The security deposit is refunded at closure, subject to the bank's conditions.

blocks.text: HDFC and Kotak refund the security deposit only to full-KYC customers, and HDFC doesn't refund it if the tag balance is negative. Banks can also use the deposit to cover unpaid tolls.

sections.heading: If you're buying a used car

items.title: Check what's on the car
items.text: Run a [FASTag status check](/tools/fastag-status) with the vehicle number to see any tags still linked to it.

items.title: Ask the seller to close their tag
items.text: If they haven't, the old tag stays linked to their account until your new one replaces it.

items.title: Remove the old sticker
items.text: Peel it off and destroy it.

items.title: Buy a new FASTag in your name
items.text: Get one from any bank, or [buy a FASTag here](/buy-fastag), and stick it correctly. See [where to stick your FASTag](/guides/where-to-stick-fastag).

blocks.text: Under the One Vehicle One FASTag rule, your new tag becomes the only active tag on that vehicle number, and older tags on it are closed.

sections.heading: OneTag isn't a transfer to a new owner

blocks.text: OneTag, live in the Rajmargyatra app since 17 September 2026, lets **the same owner** move their FASTag to a different bank and keep the tag. It doesn't change the owner. When a car changes hands, the seller still closes the tag and the buyer still gets a new one.

sections.heading: If you had an Annual Pass

blocks.text: The FASTag Annual Pass is non-transferable: it's valid only for the vehicle the tag is fixed on and registered to. NHAI hasn't published what happens to unused pass trips when a tag is closed, so ask your bank before you close it. See [FASTag Annual Pass](/guides/fastag-annual-pass).

faqs.q: Can I transfer my FASTag to a new owner when I sell my car?
faqs.a: No. The seller closes the FASTag account with their bank, and the buyer buys a new FASTag in their own name.

faqs.q: How do I close my FASTag account?
faqs.a: Contact the bank that issued it through its FASTag portal or helpline, settle any negative balance, and request closure. The unused balance is refunded to your bank account.

faqs.q: Will I get my FASTag security deposit back?
faqs.a: Usually yes, at closure, but conditions apply. For example, HDFC and Kotak refund it only to full-KYC customers, and HDFC doesn't refund it if your balance is negative.

faqs.q: I bought a used car with a FASTag already on it. Can I use it?
faqs.a: No. The tag belongs to the seller's account. Remove it and buy a new FASTag in your name; your new tag becomes the only active one on the vehicle.

title: Paying toll without a working FASTag: penalties and your rights
metaTitle: Toll without FASTag in 2026: 1.25× UPI or e-notice
description: From 10 April 2026, a vehicle without a valid FASTag pays 1.25× the toll by UPI, or gets an e-notice payable at 1× within 72 hours or 2× after. And if your valid FASTag isn't read because of the plaza, you cross free.
card: What you pay without a valid FASTag in 2026, how e-notices work, and when the plaza must let you through free.
checkedAgainst: Gazette G.S.R. 251(E), G.S.R. 191(E), G.S.R. 734(E), PIB releases
lede: The rules for toll without a FASTag changed twice in six months. Here is what applies at national highway plazas from 10 April 2026.
quickAnswer: From **10 April 2026**, a vehicle without a valid FASTag at a national highway plaza can pay **1.25 times the toll by UPI**. If it doesn't pay that way, an **e-notice** is sent to the owner: pay **1× the toll within 72 hours, or 2× after that**. But if your FASTag **is valid, has enough balance and the plaza's reader fails**, you must be allowed through **free**, with a zero-transaction receipt.

sections.heading: The rule today

head: Your situation
What you pay
rows: No FASTag, or tag not valid (blacklisted, no balance), pay by UPI
No valid FASTag and you don't pay by UPI
E-notice to the vehicle owner: 1× if paid within 72 hours, 2× after
Valid FASTag with enough balance, plaza reader fails
Nothing; you get a zero-transaction receipt
Tag not fixed on the windshield (loose or in hand)
Double the toll, and the tag can be blacklisted
blocks.note: For a ₹100 toll: ₹125 by UPI; ₹100 on an e-notice paid within 72 hours, ₹200 after.

blocks.text: A vehicle entering a fee plaza without a FASTag or a valid functional FASTag that opts to pay through UPI shall pay 1.25 times the user fee. If it doesn't opt to pay this way, it is dealt with under the unpaid-fee (e-notice) rule.

source.title: Gazette G.S.R. 251(E) – NH Fee (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026

sections.heading: When the plaza must let you through free

blocks.text: A vehicle with a valid, functional FASTag having sufficient balance that couldn't pay because the electronic toll collection equipment malfunctioned shall be allowed to cross without paying any user fee, and a zero-transaction receipt shall be issued.

source.title: Gazette G.S.R. 734(E) – NH Fee (Third Amendment) Rules, 2025

blocks.title: Your tag isn't read
blocks.text: First check your tag is valid and has balance in your bank app. If it is, tell the operator the reader failed and ask for a zero-transaction receipt instead of paying. If you're made to pay anyway, keep the receipt and complain to your bank and the 1033 helpline.

NHAI also published a guideline in 2021 for a waiting time of no more than 10 seconds per vehicle: if the queue goes beyond a yellow line 100 metres from the booth, vehicles pass without paying until the queue is back within 100 metres. It's an NHAI guideline rather than part of the fee rules, and we couldn't confirm how it's enforced in 2026.

sections.heading: How e-notices work

items.title: The passage is recorded
items.text: Cameras and the toll system record a crossing where the toll wasn't received.

items.title: The owner gets an e-notice
items.text: It goes to the owner listed in VAHAN by SMS, email or app, and is also shown on nhfeenotice.parivahan.gov.in and in the Rajmargyatra app.

items.title: Pay within 72 hours for 1×
items.text: After 72 hours the amount becomes 2× the toll.

items.title: Disagree? Object within 72 hours
items.text: Your objection must be decided within 5 days, or the claim lapses.

items.title: Don't ignore it
items.text: If it's unpaid after 15 days with no objection pending, the dues are posted on VAHAN and vehicle-related services can be restricted. Unpaid e-notices can also get your FASTag blacklisted.

blocks.text: Unpaid user fee is payable at twice the fee, or at the fee itself if paid within 72 hours of the e-notice.

source.title: Gazette G.S.R. 191(E) – unpaid user fee and e-notice

blocks.text: Barrier-free (MLFF) lanes, live at several NH plazas since May 2026, use the same e-notice process when a payment fails. See [FASTag e-notice](/fastag-e-notice) and [MLFF](/mlff).

sections.heading: How the rule changed

head: Period
Without a valid FASTag
rows: 1.25× by UPI, otherwise e-notice (1× within 72 hours, 2× after)
blocks.note: The 2026 amendment removed the 2× cash option from the rule. News reports say plazas stopped taking cash from 10 April 2026; we didn't find an NHAI statement confirming that on the ground.

faqs.q: What is the toll for a car without FASTag in 2026?
faqs.a: From 10 April 2026, 1.25 times the toll if you pay by UPI at the plaza. Otherwise an e-notice is sent: 1× if paid within 72 hours, 2× after that.

faqs.q: Can I pay toll in cash without FASTag?
faqs.a: The rules from 10 April 2026 no longer include a cash option at national highway plazas; payment is by FASTag or UPI, or through an e-notice.

faqs.q: My FASTag is valid but the plaza scanner didn't read it. Do I have to pay?
faqs.a: No. If your tag is valid and has enough balance and the plaza's equipment fails, you must be allowed through free with a zero-transaction receipt.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't pay a FASTag e-notice?
faqs.a: After 72 hours it doubles. If it's still unpaid after 15 days with no objection pending, the dues go on VAHAN and vehicle services can be restricted; your FASTag can also be blacklisted.

title: FASTag vehicle classes (VC4, VC5, VC7…) and what to do if you're overcharged
metaTitle: FASTag vehicle class list: VC4, VC5, VC7, VC12 explained
description: What VC4, VC5, VC6, VC7, VC12, VC15 and VC16 mean on a FASTag, which vehicles each covers, and what to do if your tag has the wrong class and you're charged the wrong toll.
card: VC4 to VC16 in one table, and how to fix a tag with the wrong class before it gets blacklisted.
checkedAgainst: IHMCL vehicle classification document, NHAI FAQ, NH fee notifications
lede: The class printed on your FASTag decides which toll rate you pay. A wrong class means the wrong toll, and it can get the tag blacklisted.
quickAnswer: The class on your FASTag tells the toll system what kind of vehicle you drive. **VC4** is for **cars, jeeps and vans** (and Tata Ace-type mini trucks); **VC5** for light commercial vehicles and mini-buses; **VC7** for 2-axle buses and trucks; **VC6** for 3-axle commercial vehicles; **VC12** for 4–6 axle trucks; **VC15** for 7+ axle trucks; **VC16** for earth-moving and construction machinery. If your tag shows the wrong class, ask your bank for a **replacement tag** of the right class.

sections.heading: The tag classes

head: Tag class
Vehicles
Weight (GVW) / axles
rows: Car, jeep, van; Tata Ace-type mini LCV
blocks.note: From IHMCL's FASTag issuance vehicle classification document (July 2025). FASTags aren't issued for two-wheelers, three-wheelers or tractors, and two-wheelers pay no toll on national highways.

sections.heading: How the class sets your toll

blocks.text: Toll rates on national highways are set per kilometre for six fee categories, and every plaza publishes its rates by category. The tag class maps your vehicle to one of them. The base rates fixed in 2007-08, which are revised every year, show how much the category matters:

head: Fee category
Base rate (2007-08), ₹/km
blocks.note: Base rates from NH fee notifications; actual toll is revised yearly and differs by plaza. Check a plaza's rates on its [toll plaza page](/sitemap).

sections.heading: If your tag has the wrong class

blocks.text: A car tag (VC4) on a truck underpays; a truck tag on a car overpays. The plaza system flags a mismatch between the vehicle and the tag's class, and NHAI's FAQ says such a tag is liable to be blacklisted. Since 2024, new tags are issued only after checking the vehicle against VAHAN, to stop class mismatches.

items.title: Check the class on your tag
items.text: It's printed on the FASTag and shown in your bank's app.

items.title: Ask for a replacement of the correct class
items.text: Banks treat this as a replacement. At Axis Bank it's the "mismatched" replacement, ₹100. See [replace or reissue a FASTag](/guides/fastag-replacement-reissue).

items.title: Dispute any overcharge
items.text: If you were charged a higher class's toll, raise a dispute with your bank for the difference. See [wrong or double deduction](/guides/fastag-wrong-deduction-refund).

blocks.text: Never use one vehicle's FASTag on another vehicle. It isn't allowed, and it can get the tag blacklisted.

faqs.q: What is VC4 in FASTag?
faqs.a: VC4 is the class for cars, jeeps and vans, and also Tata Ace-type mini trucks, with gross vehicle weight up to 7,500 kg.

faqs.q: Which FASTag class is for a truck?
faqs.a: It depends on the axles: VC7 for a 2-axle truck, VC6 for 3 axles, VC12 for 4 to 6 axles and VC15 for 7 or more axles.

faqs.q: What happens if my FASTag has the wrong vehicle class?
faqs.a: You may be charged the wrong toll, and the tag can be blacklisted for a class mismatch. Ask your bank for a replacement tag of the correct class.

faqs.q: Do two-wheelers need a FASTag?
faqs.a: No. FASTags aren't issued for two-wheelers, and no toll is charged from two-wheelers on national highways.

title: Toll concessions: local monthly pass, return-trip discount and exempt vehicles
metaTitle: Toll local pass, return discount & exempt vehicles
description: Live within 20 km of a toll plaza? Get a local monthly pass. Coming back within 24 hours? A return pass costs 1.5× one way. Plus the 50-trip pass, the local commercial discount and who is exempt from toll on national highways.
card: Local pass within 20 km, 24-hour return discount, 50-trip pass, and the official list of toll-exempt vehicles.
checkedAgainst: NH fee notifications, PIB releases, NHAI FAQ
lede: Many drivers pay the full one-way toll every time without knowing about the passes that already exist. Here's every concession on national highway plazas, and how to get it.
quickAnswer: If you **live within 20 km of a toll plaza** and use a private vehicle, you can get a **local monthly pass** with unlimited crossings of that plaza, now also on the **Rajmargyatra app** at many plazas. A **return trip within 24 hours** costs **1.5× the one-way toll**. Regular commuters can buy a **50-trip pass** valid for a month at **two-thirds** of 50 single trips. Some official and emergency vehicles are **exempt** from toll altogether.

Who
Price
Valid for
rows: Private vehicle, owner living within 20 km of the plaza

blocks.note: From NH fee notifications (e.g. Gazette S.O. 1157(E), March 2026). Local pass rates differ by plaza; check the rate shown at your plaza.

sections.heading: Getting a local monthly pass

items: **Who qualifies:** a non-commercial vehicle whose owner lives within 20 km of the plaza.
**Where it's not available:** where the toll is collected under a closed system, or where a service road or alternative road exists.
**At the plaza:** apply at the plaza helpdesk with your Aadhaar, RC and proof of address.

**Online:** since July 2026 you can apply in the **Rajmargyatra app** at participating plazas (121 by 18 August 2026). The app checks your documents through DigiLocker and VAHAN, and your address against the 20 km radius.

blocks.title: Daily commuter
blocks.text: If you cross the same plaza twice a day, compare the local pass rate with your monthly tolls. A local pass at that plaza also means those crossings don't count against an Annual Pass.

sections.heading: Who is exempt from toll

blocks.text: Rule 11 of the National Highways Fee Rules lists the exempt categories. In short:

items: **Constitutional and senior office holders**, including the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Governors, Chief Justice of India and Supreme Court judges, Union ministers, Chief Ministers, the Lok Sabha Speaker, High Court judges, MPs and MLAs/MLCs, the Chief Secretary of a state and Secretaries to the Government of India, plus foreign dignitaries on state visits.
**Gallantry award winners**: Param Vir Chakra, Ashok Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra and Shaurya Chakra.
**On official duty**: Ministry of Defence vehicles, Central and State armed forces in uniform, paramilitary forces and police, and Executive Magistrates.
**Emergency and highway vehicles**: fire-fighting vehicles, ambulances, funeral vans, and NHAI or government vehicles used for highway inspection, survey, construction or operation.
**Vehicles specially designed for persons with physical disability.**

blocks.text: The exemption applies only when the vehicle is used for an official purpose; for example, army personnel commuting in private cars aren't exempt. Exempt vehicles must still carry a FASTag, issued free as an exempt tag through NHAI's authorised agency.
There's no exemption for public carriers such as buses and taxis.

sections.heading: Two more discounts worth knowing

items: **Partly opened national expressways:** from 15 February 2026 (for one year or until fully opened), the normal NH toll is charged instead of the higher expressway rate.

**Highways being widened:** where a 2-lane road with paved shoulders is being upgraded to 4 or more lanes, users pay 50% of the earlier toll until the work is complete (MoRTH, announced January 2026).

faqs.q: Is toll free for local residents near a toll plaza?
faqs.a: Not free, but residents within 20 km using a private vehicle can get a local monthly pass with unlimited crossings of that plaza, at a fixed monthly rate set per plaza.

faqs.q: Is there a discount on a return journey at a toll plaza?
faqs.a: Yes. A return pass costs 1.5 times the one-way toll and covers the return trip within 24 hours of payment.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a toll local pass online?
faqs.a: Use the Rajmargyatra app at participating plazas; it verifies documents through DigiLocker and VAHAN and checks you live within 20 km. Otherwise apply at the plaza helpdesk with Aadhaar, RC and proof of address.

faqs.q: Who is exempt from paying toll?
faqs.a: Categories in Rule 11 of the NH Fee Rules: senior office holders and gallantry award winners, defence, armed forces and police on official duty, fire-fighting vehicles, ambulances, funeral vans, highway vehicles on duty and vehicles specially designed for persons with disability.
